annotation.title_clean: Case-Based Robotic Architecture with Multiple Underlying Ethical Frameworks for Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.title_en: Case-Based Robotic Architecture with Multiple Underlying Ethical Frameworks for Human-Robot Interaction
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Chen, S.; Arkin, R.C.; Borenstein, J.; Wagner, A.R.; Cruz, A.M.
annotation.venue: ICRES 2022: 7th International Conference on Robot Ethics and Standards
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper proposing a case-based reasoning architecture letting a robot choose actions using cases from multiple ethical frameworks (folk morality, utilitarianism, Kantian, care, virtue, justice). Implemented on an NAO robot in a pill-sorting task for older adults, deciding whether to give false encouragement.
key_provisions_or_claims: No agreed moral theory exists, so a single fixed ethical framework is impractical for robots.
Architecture uses case-based reasoning with cases derived from surveys of laypeople and ethics experts.
Case selection module picks the most relevant case; action selection module chooses the action.
Implemented on an NAO robot for robotic deception in pill sorting with older adults.
Architecture can be extended with more situational variables and gestures.
